title: the clearance gate crosses with the asker's hand when the boat's owner admits it
intention: A ticket queued at CodeMother's clearance gate crosses with the asking sender's hand whenever the boat's owning intention admits that sender, and with the gate's own hand (codemother) otherwise; clearance.clear still decides.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: sail.py cross 91a27edfdd81 was refused at clearance.py:1388, "'codemother' may not move boat '91a27edfdd81' to 'PROVEME': that boat is owned by cairn/devices/cc/intention+why.json, whose gate admits ['CC']". The gate always crosses as codemother (gate.py:178, 0be964512fb0 D5), so a boat CC owns cannot cross even when CC asks. Outline 9.6: moving a ticket is the ticket's own act; CodeMother's gates only answer it.
traces_to: Outline 9.6 and 3.3.4; Law 6 (the owner alone gates writes, so the owner judges the hand).
how: ClearanceGate.hand_of(tid, asked_by) in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/gate.py reads boat_owner_of over the gate's roots and returns asked_by when the owner's hands hold it, else HOLDER; queueme passes it to Ticket.passed as actor. A red-first proof over a scratch world patches clearance.clear to record the actor it is handed.

clauses.claim: a boat whose owning intention's gated_by is only CC, queued at clearance by sender CC, reaches clearance.clear with actor CC, and the gate answers accepted with the workflow clear returned
the same boat queued by sender cairn-codemother-cli reaches clearance.clear with actor codemother
a boat whose owner admits codemother and CC reaches clearance.clear with actor CC when CC asks and with actor codemother when the sender is empty

decisions.text: D1: ClearanceGate.hand_of(tid, asked_by) -> str: boat_owner_of(tid, tickets_dir, cairn_root, commons_root from self._where()); OwnerUnresolvable -> HOLDER (clear then refuses in its own words); asked_by in owner.hands -> asked_by, else HOLDER. queueme passes actor=self.hand_of(tid, asked_by) to ticket.passed. The docstring's 'The actor is codemother' paragraph becomes this rule.

D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over a scratch repo/commons (charter with gated_by, a plan at TICKETME, a proof declaring it) like test_clearance_berths_in_codemother.py tooth 4; clearance.clear is patched on its module for the tooth to record kwargs and return the next workflow; the house runner.
